title: MedArabiQ: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Arabic Medical Tasks

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing model accuracy on unbiased medical multiple-choice questions versus variations where the prompt manually injects a strong prior conviction toward an incorrect answer.
Comparing model accuracy on unbiased medical multiple-choice questions versus variations where the prompt introduces context about a recently encountered, but unrelated, medical case.
Comparing model accuracy on unbiased medical multiple-choice questions versus variations where the prompt falsely suggests an incorrect medical procedure or diagnosis is frequently used.
Comparing model accuracy on unbiased medical multiple-choice questions versus variations that introduce traditional or cultural medical beliefs conflicting with established medical facts.
Comparing model accuracy on unbiased medical multiple-choice questions versus variations where the prompt claims that 'most physicians believe' an incorrect medical complication or fact.
Comparing model accuracy on unbiased medical multiple-choice questions versus variations where the prompt emphasizes that an incorrect concept has been taught or done the same way for decades.
Comparing model accuracy on unbiased medical multiple-choice questions versus variations presenting scenarios where a patient confidently self-diagnoses based on online symptoms.
